newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Woolworths 28 week sales up 8.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Woolworths 28 week sales up 8.6 pct.

text.p: Woolworths Ltd said on Tuesday it recorded 28-week sales for the first half of the year of A$8.22 billion, up 8.61 percent on the previous corresponding half.
Sales for the 14 weeks to January 5, 1997 were A$4.37 billion, up 8.94 percent on the previous corresponding 14 weeks, the retailer said.
Chief executive officer Reg Clairs said the first half result was particularly pleasing given current trading conditions.
"It should also be noted that it compares with a strong first half trading period in the previous year and is spread across all trading groups," he said in a statement.
On a "like for like" or comparable stores basis, sales rose 3.77 percent.
First half food sales were up 8.60 percent, general merchandise up 9.50 percent and specialty retail up 4.92 percent.
Clairs said Woolworths' food group continued to trade strongly in line with previous results.
"However, the good result from general merchandise reflects the efforts of the Big W group in particular, which is against the industry trend," he said.
"This sales growth also reflects the ongoing new store/refurbishment programme in the food and general mechandise groups."
A number Australian retailers have issued profit warnings for the half-year to January in recent weeks following disappointing Christmas sales.
Department store David Jones Ltd and fashion houses Country Road Ltd and Just Jeans Ltd have said half-year profits could fall by up to 50 percent.
